summary: Adds a new EQL 3.0.6 upgrade self-edge (20261002T0000_upgrade_eql_v3_3_0_6) to @cipherstash/stack-prisma and re-emits the v3 baseline migration so it bakes the 3.0.6 install SQL (sha256 9b6dab78…) and carries a fifth no-SQL invariant carrier op; the head ref now requires the 3.0.6 invariant. The PR deliberately lands before the Version Packages PR (#938) that bumps @cipherstash/eql 3.0.5 → 3.0.6, so at head the in-tree @cipherstash/eql is still 3.0.5 (manifest accde003…) while the baseline bakes 3.0.6 bytes that nothing in-tree attests; the eqlVersion marker test was loosened to accept both. The released artefacts change a published baseline identity (1.1.x 10306543… → 2fdc7caf…) and add one more DROP SCHEMA eql_v3 CASCADE reinstall to every existing database's upgrade path. The functional SQL difference is the version stamp only (verified in the baked bytes). Offline stack-prisma tests ran and passed in CI; the live apply suite that executes the baked SQL did not run in CI. The material risks are release-ordering with #938, stale vendored migration spaces in consumer repos, and the reinstall cascade on existing databases — all documented by the change, none high-impact on their own.

behaviour_changes.description: New data-class self-edge migration 20261002T0000_upgrade_eql_v3_3_0_6 re-executes the full ~2.6 MB EQL install SQL (which begins with DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS eql_v3 CASCADE and eql_v3_internal CASCADE) on every existing database that lacks the 3.0.6 invariant, with postchecks for version '3.0.6', the schema comment, and eql_v3.query_json.

The published baseline migration 20260601T0100_install_eql_v3_bundle is re-emitted: its baked SQL moves to eql-3.0.6, a fifth additive carrier op is added, existing carrier postchecks now check '3.0.6', and migrationHash changes bad30c9b… → 2fdc7caf… (npm 1.1.x shipped 10306543…). createdAt is unchanged.

The contract-space head ref (and the control descriptor) now requires invariant cipherstash:upgrade-eql-v3-bundle-3.0.6-v1, so every existing database must walk the new edge on the next migrate; 1.0.0/1.1.x databases walk the 3.0.5 and 3.0.6 edges, reinstalling the bundle twice.

The migration baking 3.0.6 lands on main while the in-tree @cipherstash/eql is still 3.0.5; the eqlVersion marker test accepts either 3.0.5 or 3.0.6, and the live byte-identity check is documented as red until #938 merges. Correct release depends on #938 merging after this PR with a 3.0.6 bundle whose digest equals 9b6dab78….
Changesets, README, DEVELOPING.md, packages/eql/AGENTS.md and the shipped stash-prisma agent skill updated to describe 3.0.6, the double reinstall and the stale-vendored-space remedy.
Offline tests re-pinned to the new hashes and extended for the 3.0.6 edge and paths; the live Postgres suite gains a db-init case and a 3.0.4→3.0.5→3.0.6 walk executing the baked SQL.

failure_scenarios.title: Baked 3.0.6 bytes and the eventual @cipherstash/eql 3.0.6 release drift apart, or release order is inverted
failure_scenarios.trigger: #938 is regenerated with further EQL SQL changes before merging (so its 3.0.6 install digest is no longer 9b6dab78…), or a stack-prisma release is cut from main before #938 merges.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: At head the in-tree manifest is eql 3.0.5 / accde003… (E-9), yet the baseline and new edge bake 9b6dab78… (E-6). Those bytes are pinned only against themselves in PUBLISHED_MIGRATIONS; the lockstep test passes at head only because the 3.0.5 edge still bakes accde003… (E-10), and the eqlVersion marker accepts both versions (E-11). Provenance of 9b6dab78… rests on the PR's account of emitting against #938's files (E-19).
failure_scenarios.consequence: Case 1: the lockstep test fails on #938 (loud) and a further migration plus another baseline re-pin is needed. Case 2: a stack-prisma release would pin @cipherstash/eql 3.0.5 exactly while db init installs a bundle stamped 3.0.6, so the CLI/stack installer and the Prisma migrations disagree on the installed version for those users, and the frozen artefact cannot be corrected without another re-emit.

failure_scenarios.title: Consumers with a stale vendored migrations/cipherstash/ fail db init or silently stay on the old bundle
failure_scenarios.trigger: A consumer upgrades to the release carrying this change without deleting migrations/cipherstash/, or runs migrate/db init without migration plan first. Also applies to spaces vendored from main at the unpublished 3.0.5 baseline (bad30c9b…).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The baseline's identity changes again (E-4, E-5). The seed phase keeps an existing baseline directory but overwrites refs/head.json, which now also requires the 3.0.6 invariant (E-8). A stale genesis edge does not carry it, so db init (additive-only) must plan the data-class 3.0.6 self-edge and is refused; without a seed run the new edges are never on disk (E-18).
failure_scenarios.consequence: Fresh-database db init fails with a POLICY_VIOLATION naming only an op id; migrate without plan leaves the database on the older bundle without warning. The bundle difference is only the version stamp, so no functional or data effect beyond the failed or skipped run.

failure_scenarios.title: The 3.0.6 reinstall drops objects that depend on eql_v3 on every existing database, for a version-stamp-only release
failure_scenarios.trigger: prisma-next migrate against an existing database (1.x from npm, or one already at 3.0.5 built from main) that has functional indexes, RLS policies, views or constraints referencing eql_v3 / eql_v3_internal objects.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The new edge executes the full install SQL (E-1), which begins with DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS eql_v3 CASCADE and eql_v3_internal CASCADE (E-3). 1.0.0/1.1.x databases walk the 3.0.5 and 3.0.6 edges in one run (E-2), reinstalling twice.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Dependent customer objects are dropped without error: ORE/HMAC indexes disappear (queries degrade to scans, unique constraints backed by them stop being enforced) and RLS policies calling eql_v3 functions are removed until the customer recreates them. Upgrade runs take longer, and DDL locks are held longer. For npm users this cascade already happened once with the 3.0.5 edge at base; the new exposure is databases already at 3.0.5 and the second reinstall.

failure_scenarios.mitigation: Release notes already say to recreate indexes and grants after migrate (E-13); state explicitly that 3.0.6 changes only the version stamp, so recreating is the only action. Consider running the live migration suite in CI with a seeded table and index.

recommended_controls.description: Before publishing, confirm #938's release-manifest installSqlSha256 is 9b6dab78… and its lockstep test is green; publish stack-prisma and @cipherstash/eql together from #938.
Narrow the eqlVersion marker to '3.0.6' and make the live byte-identity check green right after #938 merges (follow-up named in the PR).
Run migration-apply-live-pg against Postgres in CI (or once manually on the #938 branch), ideally with a table carrying an ORE/HMAC index, to confirm the end state and record what the cascade drops.
In the 1.2.0 release notes, lead with the vendored-directory delete + migration plan step and the post-migrate index/grant/RLS recreation; update skills/stash-supabase once 3.0.6 ships.
Review the baseline re-emit decision itself (third re-pin of a frozen digest) against the append-only rule, and confirm createdAt is unchanged.
